title: Two Questions: what intelligence is, and how we measure it | Doing and Feeling 1/14
description:
Doing and Feeling: Intelligence and Consciousness in Depth, episode 1 of 14.

The series opens with its two questions, doing and feeling, then takes a careful look at IQ: the general factor g, what test scores predict, what heritability does and doesn't mean, the Flynn effect, group differences, and the field's eugenic history.

title: Minds in Other Bodies: crows, octopuses, bees, cells and swarms | Doing and Feeling 2/14
description:
Doing and Feeling: Intelligence and Consciousness in Depth, episode 2 of 14.

Intelligence evolved more than once, on very different hardware. A tour of crows, octopuses, bees, single cells, plants and swarms, and of the two errors science makes about animal minds: seeing too much, like Clever Hans, and too little.

title: Intelligence, Formally: prediction, compression and the measure of a mind | Doing and Feeling 3/14

title: Life as Computation: from self-copying code to social minds | Doing and Feeling 4/14
description:
Doing and Feeling: Intelligence and Consciousness in Depth, episode 4 of 14.

The strongest case that life, intelligence and computation form one continuum, built on Blaise Aguera y Arcas's What Is Intelligence?: self-copying code, symbiogenesis, the physics of prediction, regulation and social minds. Then the case is tested against the objection that, on a loose enough definition, everything computes.

title: The Evidence: what we can measure, and how sure we are | Doing and Feeling 10/14
description:
Doing and Feeling: Intelligence and Consciousness in Depth, episode 10 of 14.

What the science of consciousness can actually measure: neural correlates, no-report methods, blindsight and neglect, split brains, hidden awareness in unresponsive patients, the zap-and-zip complexity index, anesthesia, sleep, psychedelics, meditation, free will experiments and animal minds. Some famous findings turn out shakier than their reputations.

Could today's AI be conscious? What can actually be checked: the indicator method, probabilistic frameworks, interpretability evidence, what the subject would even be, and why self-reports are hard to trust. The episode ends with the strongest case for machine consciousness.
